comparator.name: Media and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught route has 60 EC of first-year media study, 24 EC of common second-year courses plus three 12 EC choices, and 42 EC of open electives plus an 18 EC thesis seminar. The example selects Film Studies in each choice group.

components.name: Living Information
components.note: The first year also includes an uncredited literacy test, tutoring and academic writing. Academic writing is taught through Media Research.

components.name: Media Research
components.note: Builds on Media Aesthetics and introduces research design, sources and academic writing.

components.name: Film Analysis
components.note: Requires positive binding study advice. Media Aesthetics prepares students for film analysis and the video essay.

components.name: Film Practices
components.note: Requires positive binding study advice. The guide recommends passing Media Aesthetics before this production course.

components.name: Advanced Topics in Media and Culture: Film
components.note: Requires positive binding study advice. The guide recommends passing Media Aesthetics, Media Theory and Media Research first.

components.name: Philosophy of the Humanities 2 (Media and Culture)
components.note: Builds on Philosophy of the Humanities 1, which is offered in the preceding block.

components.name: Free-choice electives, minor, internship or study abroad
components.note: Choose electives, a minor, an approved placement or study abroad. Courses taken at another institution require Examination Board approval.

components.name: Research Seminar and Bachelor's Thesis Media and Culture
components.note: Pass the first-year courses and the compulsory second-year courses before starting. Film Practices is exempt from the entry requirement but remains part of the degree. The seminar and thesis are completed within one semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three options cover broad media history and representation, film adaptation and visual storytelling, and cross-media audiences and public communication. Their different emphases are supported by the scheduled courses.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both analyse how narrative, sound and image produce meaning. UvA applies these tools across a wider range of media objects.
Both examine historical changes in media technologies and their cultural effects. UCR studies the material history of media from print to digital networks.
Both include practical documentary production. UvA also covers fiction production and its associated workflows.
Both use close analysis of film form. UCR centres on adaptations, while UvA also uses frameworks such as auteur, genre and spectator theory.
Both develop research design and qualitative interpretation. UCR applies these methods to social questions, while UvA includes methods and sources specific to media.
